1.explanation:
• packages/components/src/components/button/button.config.js: This file defines the CSS custom-property tokens and style mappings for each button size. It needs entries for the new "large" and "xl" heights so the generated CSS will include the correct rem values (8rem and 10rem).
• packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.js: This is the React implementation that switches on the size prop and applies the corresponding CSS class. It must be updated to recognize "large" and "xl" and map them to the new CSS classes.
• packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.test.js: The unit tests currently only cover existing sizes. Tests should be added or updated to assert that size="large" and size="xl" produce the correct class names and render heights.
• packages/react/src/components/Button/Button-story.js: The Storybook stories need examples for the two new size variants so designers and engineers can preview the buttons in the docs.
• packages/react/src/components/Button/Button.mdx: The component MDX documentation still lists only "field", "small", and "default" under the size prop. It must be updated to include "large" and "xl" with their specs and REM/px values.
1.bug_scenario: The ask is to add two new size variants—"xl" (80px / 10rem tall) and "large" (64px / 8rem tall)—to the React Button component so that <Button size="xl"> and <Button size="large"> render correctly. Currently the component only recognizes "default", "field", and "small", so requesting "xl" or "large" silently falls back to the default height, and neither the CSS config nor the MDX documentation or stories/tests include these sizes.

2.explanation:
• button.config.js defines the configurable size tokens (height, padding, font sizes) used by the vanilla JS/CSS implementation. We need to add entries for “large” and “xl” here so styles get generated.

• button.js in the components package applies those tokens and maps size names to CSS class names. It must recognize the new variants and output the right class.

• Button.js in the React wrapper reads the size prop and passes it through as a className or styled variant. It currently only handles “field”, “small”, and default — it must be updated to accept “large” and “xl”.

• Button-test.js needs new unit tests asserting that <Button size=“large”> and <Button size=“xl”> render with the correct className and computed inline styles (height and padding).

• Button-story.js (storybook) must demonstrate the two new size variants in the Button gallery so designers and engineers see them in the preview.

• Button.mdx (the docs) must be updated to list “large” and “xl” in the Component API > Button size section with the correct values (8rem/10rem).  This ensures the documentation and prop tables are accurate for consumers.
2.bug_scenario: The team needs to support two new Button size variants in the Carbon React Button component — an extra-large (“xl”) at 80px (10rem) tall and a “large” at 64px (8rem) tall. The screenshots show the proposed keyboard / wizard flow uses 80px high primary calls-to-action, and modal footer buttons use 64px high secondary/secondary buttons in line with existing modal button styles. Currently, the Button only supports “default” (42px), “field”, and “small” sizes. When rendering <Button size=“xl”> or <Button size=“large”>, the component must apply the correct height, padding, font sizing, and class names so that the new variants match the spec.
